product: DJI Power 1000 V2 (the current model; it replaced the original Power 1000)

wins.need: The most 1 kWh power station for the money
wins.claim: Costs less per measured usable watt-hour than the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 (arithmetic: today's price ÷ OutdoorGearLab's measured usable AC Wh)
wins.who: OutdoorGearLab (Kenji Mowrey), measured usable Wh; prices from Amazon and the EcoFlow and BLUETTI stores

wins.need: Running high-watt appliances and corded tools
wins.claim: The US model is rated for more AC current than the rated continuous output of the DELTA 3 (1,800 W), the Elite 100 V2 (1,800 W) or the Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 (1,500 W). A named tester ran an 1,800 W mitre saw on it
wins.figure: DJI lists the DYM1000V2L AC output at 100–120 V, max 20 A (arithmetic: 20 A × 120 V = 2,400 W). The Technology Man ran a Bosch 1,800 W sliding mitre saw, a 14-inch induction bandsaw and a 12,000 BTU portable AC. His UK 230 V unit beeped at about 2,900 W and cut out just over 3,000 W
wins.who: DJI spec page; The Technology Man

wins.need: Start with 1 kWh and grow it later
wins.claim: Expands further than the EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1–5 kWh per EcoFlow). The Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 (up to 11 kWh) matches it
wins.figure: Up to five DJI Power Expansion Battery 2000 packs (2,048 Wh each), 11,264 Wh in total, through the SDC port

wins.claim: Charges about twice as fast as the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 in OutdoorGearLab's test. The DELTA 3 and Anker C1000 Gen 2 charged faster
wins.figure: DJI 1,041 Wh/hr, full in 59 min; Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 563 Wh/hr; Elite 100 V2 512 Wh/hr; Anker C1000 Gen 2 1,097 Wh/hr; DELTA 3 1,229 Wh/hr

wins.need: Quiet operation in a bedroom or campsite
wins.claim: Low measured noise while fast charging. OutdoorGearLab lists 'Runs very quietly' as a pro (no rival measured with the same method)
wins.figure: About 37 dB at 1 m while charging at over 1,400 W (The Technology Man). DJI claims 26 dB

wins.need: Charging DJI drones and laptops in the field
wins.claim: Dual 140 W USB-C ports, tested at full power at the same time. It also fast-charged a drone battery in OutdoorGearLab's test
wins.figure: 280 W combined over two USB-C ports (The Technology Man). Drone battery 10% to 95% in 'just over 30 minutes' (OutdoorGearLab)

weak.claim: Heaviest of the five ~1 kWh units OutdoorGearLab weighed
weak.figure: 31.5 lb, against Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 24.4 lb, Elite 100 V2 25.0 lb, Anker C1000 Gen 2 25.2 lb and DELTA 3 28.1 lb. Arithmetic: 27.9 usable Wh/lb against 31.0–37.3 for the others

weak.claim: Solar and 12 V charging need DJI's proprietary adapters. The built-in route takes 400 W through an add-on MPPT module, while the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 has a built-in 1,000 W MPPT input
weak.figure: Solar Panel Adapter Module up to 400 W; up to 1,200 W solar only with the separate 1.8 kW charger. OutdoorGearLab says the proprietary ports 'can be a deal-breaker'. In bright, high cloud, The Technology Man got just under 70 W from a 120 W panel

weak.claim: Ranked below the Anker, EcoFlow and Jackery units in OutdoorGearLab's overall test
weak.figure: Overall 66, ranked 8th of 14 (Anker C1000 Gen 2 70; DELTA 3 67; Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 67). Power output sub-score 5.7

weak.claim: High idle draw with the inverter on, and poor DC efficiency
weak.figure: About 23 W idle with the inverter on and no load (100% to 73% in 12 h). DC output delivered 789 Wh (about 77%)

weak.claim: Could not start an induction-motor table saw
weak.figure: The start-up draw triggered overload protection

weak.claim: Low pass-through power while plugged in (US model)
weak.figure: Bypass AC output max 12 A (arithmetic: 1,440 W at 120 V)

weak.claim: No DJI US product page or US store listing; DronEDJ reported the V2 was not coming to the US. US warranty and support for Amazon buyers are not clear
weak.figure: us.store.dji.com/product/dji-power-1000-v2 returned 404, and dji.com sends US visitors from the V2 page to a 404. OutdoorGearLab lists a 3-year warranty, while DJI's UK FAQ says five years

weak.claim: No weatherproof rating; the AC outlets are spaced too close together
weak.figure: The Technology Man lists no weatherproof rating as a con. OutdoorGearLab lists 'AC ports are spaced too close together'

wins_for: Buyers who want about 1 kWh at the lowest price per usable watt-hour today
Running 1,500–1,800 W kitchen appliances or corded tools such as a mitre saw from a 1 kWh box
DJI drone and camera users who want 140 W USB-C and DJI fast charging
Buyers who plan to add batteries later (up to 11,264 Wh)
not_for: Solar-first campers: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (built-in 1,000 W MPPT, 25.0 lb measured)
Carrying it any distance: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (24.4 lb measured) or Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (25.2 lb)
The fastest wall recharge: EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1,229 Wh/hr measured)
Buyers who want US maker-store support and a clear US warranty: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (OutdoorGearLab's Best Buy pick) or EcoFlow DELTA 3
Running a fridge for days from the DC outputs (77% DC efficiency measured)

rivals.price: $529.99, Amazon B0FN7MSY4L, read 2026-11-15 (titled 'Solar powered Generator'; check that it is the standalone unit)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Lighter (25.2 lb vs 31.5 lb), faster wall charge (1,097 vs 1,041 Wh/hr), higher OutdoorGearLab score (70 vs 66) and the Best Buy award (OutdoorGearLab)
Fastest wall charge (1,229 Wh/hr), 3.4 lb lighter (OutdoorGearLab)
Built-in 1,000 W MPPT solar input with no adapter (BLUETTI), 6.5 lb lighter, more usable Wh (890 vs 880) (OutdoorGearLab)

rivals.price: standalone price not read; Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 + 2×100 W panels $849, Amazon B0D66VD3X4, read 2026-11-15
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Lightest (24.4 lb) and most usable Wh (910) of the five, best Wh per lb (37.3) (OutdoorGearLab)
Matches the 11 kWh expansion at 23.8 lb (Jackery's figure); under 10 ms UPS

targets.headline: The 1,000 Wh power station that gives you the most power per dollar
targets.why_it_wins_there: Arithmetic: $0.45 per measured usable Wh against $0.56–0.67 for the Elite 100 V2, Anker C1000 Gen 2 and DELTA 3 (OutdoorGearLab measurements, prices read 2026-11-15). Rated 20 A AC output on the US model

targets.headline: DJI's power station: where it beats Anker, EcoFlow and Jackery, and where it doesn't
targets.why_it_wins_there: It is DJI's 1 kWh model and the one Amazon US lists; the original Power 1000 no longer appears in Amazon search. The page should be honest about weight (31.5 lb) and solar adapters (OutdoorGearLab)

targets.search: best portable power station for home backup
targets.headline: A home backup battery you can start small and grow to 11 kWh
targets.why_it_wins_there: Up to 11,264 Wh with five 2,048 Wh packs, against 5 kWh for the DELTA 3 (DJI FAQ; EcoFlow store). Arithmetic: expansion pack $699 for 2,048 Wh = $0.34/Wh. Only a modest win: the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 matches the 11 kWh, and DJI's US support is unclear

record.asin_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 Portable Power Station, 1024Wh LFP Battery
record.name: DJI Power 1000 V2 Portable Power Station (1,024 Wh, 2,600 W)
specs: 100–120 V, 50/60 Hz, max 20 A; 4 AC outlets
100–120 V, max 13 A; 0–80% in 37 min, full in 56 min (DJI)
2 × USB-C up to 140 W each; 2 × USB-A up to 24 W each
SDC 32–58.4 V, max 60 A; SDC Lite max 8 A (solar and car need DJI adapters)
Up to 5 × Expansion Battery 2000, 11,264 Wh total
record.warranty: DJI's UK FAQ says 'the default warranty period is five years' (https://www.dji.com/uk/power-1000-v2/faq?set_region=GB). DJI has no US page for this model and OutdoorGearLab lists 3 years, so US cover for Amazon buyers needs checking
record.returns: Amazon's return terms for this listing were not read (Amazon blocked the page). DJI's US store does not list the product
record.summary: A 1 kWh LFP power station with a 20 A AC output on the US model and dual 140 W USB-C. It expands to 11 kWh with DJI batteries and is the cheapest per measured usable watt-hour of the ~1 kWh units OutdoorGearLab tested.
record.fit: Buyers who want the most 1 kWh power for the money, need to run 1,500–1,800 W appliances or tools, or use DJI drones and cameras. Not for solar-first or weight-sensitive camping.
caveats: Heaviest of OutdoorGearLab's five ~1 kWh units at 31.5 lb (OutdoorGearLab)
Solar and 12 V charging need DJI's proprietary adapters; 400 W solar through the MPPT module (DJI FAQ; OutdoorGearLab)
About 23 W idle draw with the inverter on (The Technology Man)
Could not start an induction-motor table saw (The Technology Man)
Not sold on DJI's US store, so US warranty and support need confirming (DronEDJ; us.store.dji.com 404)

unsourced: Amazon seller: amzcheck has no seller field, and three WebFetch tries at the Amazon page (dp, gp/product, aod offers) returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-15. asin_seller is left null; confirm that DJI or Amazon sells it before linking.

DJI's US product page: dji.com/us/power-1000-v2 redirects to a 404 and us.store.dji.com/product/dji-power-1000-v2 returns 404, so the official_page is DJI's UK page, which lists the US model DYM1000V2L.

US rated continuous output in watts: DJI's spec page gives only 20 A, and the UK page says '2600 W' without saying whether it is continuous. The English user manual PDF downloaded but could not be converted to text here.
Amazon return window for B0H2MFBDZL: page walled.
Standalone Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 price: Jackery's store search and Amazon search showed only bundles and the HomePower models.
Anker store price for the C1000 Gen 2: storecheck on anker.com returned HTTP 404. The Amazon price is used instead, with a title that may describe a bundle.
Rivals' USB-C wattage: I didn't look this up, so the USB-C win isn't compared against rivals.
